title: High school in North Little Rock and a semester at Gibbs High
summary: He briefly changes to Gibbs High in Little Rock hoping to join a school band, finds he must own an instrument, and returns home as tuition begins.

venues.name: North Little Rock Colored High School

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: I was going to high school then. The Armistice was signed in 1919, if I'm correct. I think it was 1919. And I was going to high school in North Little Rock. They called it the North Little Rock Colored High School. And I heard -- in 1920 I heard about a high school in Little Rock, Arkansas where they had a band -- the school had a band, and I got the impression that if you went to that school and you wanted to play in the band they would buy you an instrument.
So, I knew some friends who had moved to Little Rock
in the 3200 block on Main Street, and I asked them could I use their address because I wanted to change schools. And they said yes.

I changed school and went to Gibbs High School for one semester. But I found out that if you wanted to be in the band you had to have your own instrument. And I admired the various ones who were playing the band in the band. And I just said to myself, 'One of these days I just hope I'll be able to buy an instrument and play in the band.'

I went to high school there for that semester, and then I came on back over to my home town and went back to my regular school. And shortly after that things got so rough in my home town until they started charging tuition to go to high school. I just forget how much the tuition was. I think it was $1.50 or $2.00 a month, or something like that.
